talks.title: IT Ops Query: Ex-HashiCorp CEO's Startup Seeks '2.0 Moment' in AI Governance
talks.teaser: Industry experts analyze emerging threats surrounding IT Ops Query: Ex-HashiCorp CEO's Startup Seeks '2.0 Moment' in AI Governance.
talks.summary:
Overview: Former HashiCorp CEO Dave McDaniel discusses co-founding Dome Systems on the IT Ops Query podcast, focusing on AI agent governance after HashiCorp's $6.4 billion IBM acquisition.

Key Topics: The architectural shift from deterministic code to non-deterministic AI agent invocations; Dome's agent registry, MCP gateway, and LLM broker; and why AI governance requires new operational paradigms.

Technical Details: McDaniel explains that traditional software topology differs fundamentally from AI agents where a person calls code that calls a model with variable outputs. Dome provides centralized governance across this new topology.

Takeaways: AI agents represent a new architectural layer requiring dedicated governance infrastructure. Organizations need registries, gateways, and brokers to manage access and maintain operational control.

talks.title: The Future of Enterprise AI Agents: Governance, Security, & Scale
talks.teaser: Security researchers examine technical aspects of The Future of Enterprise AI Agents: Governance, Security, & Scale.
talks.summary:
Enterprise AI Agent Platforms

Michael Clark of Google Cloud discusses building and governing enterprise AI agents on the Gemini enterprise agent platform. He traces his path from privacy and discriminative AI at Meta to agent infrastructure, viewing agents as integrating the full technology stack.

Interoperability and Openness

He argues interoperability, openness, and transparency are essential for agent ecosystems. Connections via MCP, agent-to-agent protocols, legacy APIs, and skills determine whether recursive, self-improving agents can integrate into business processes.

Platform Architecture

Google's platform spans the Agent Development Kit, hosting runtimes, context tools, and dedicated governance plus optimization and evaluation layers. The same infrastructure supports first-party Google products and external enterprise developers.

Consumer vs. Enterprise Governance

Consumer and enterprise products face different data obligations—regulations like GDPR versus internally defined risk tolerance—but both require similar governance concepts. Clark notes enterprise release cycles differ from consumer products because of compliance and accountability requirements.

talks.title: Enterprise Apps Unpacked: Harnessing AI To Combat AI-Driven Candidate Fraud
talks.teaser: Security researchers examine technical aspects of Enterprise Apps Unpacked: Harnessing AI To Combat AI-Driven Candidate Fraud.
talks.summary:
Rising Candidate Fraud

Avature CEO Dmitri Boland tells Informa TechTarget that AI enables resume tailoring, application flooding, interview cheating, and impersonation—from unsophisticated ChatGPT use to state-actor remote hiring schemes.

Business and Security Risks

Hiring unqualified staff causes operational mistakes. Larger applicant pools also leak company technology stacks and processes to corporate spies, with North Korean remote-worker infiltration as a prominent threat.

HR Response Patterns

Customers serving banks, governments, and critical infrastructure see extensive fraud. Many shift administrative screening to AI so recruiters can meet candidates in person without ChatGPT assistance.

AI as Defender

Boland argues employers need AI scorecards and structured interviews to match candidate scale, detect inconsistencies, and separate authentic applicants from sophisticated infiltration attempts.

talks.summary:
Setting

TechTarget's Kelsey Song interviews senior writer Beth Pariseau from VMware Explore 2026 in Las Vegas on top headlines and conference themes.

Product and migration

Broadcom's VCF consolidation leaves customers facing VCF 8 end-of-support (Oct 2027) and non-trivial VCF 9 migrations across thousands of VMs; clearer Kubernetes inclusion with Tanzu (connected but separate) drew renewed attendee interest—one buyer called VCF 9.1 what everybody wanted.

AI and partnerships

Roadmap mentions Agility Ops automation for infrastructure; industry gossip centered on Nvidia's reduced keynote/session presence despite Broadcom insisting the partnership continues and supporting Nemotron models.

Private cloud narrative

Broadcom leaders claim a private-cloud/AI tipping point and public cloud PTSD, but independent analysts and customer sessions still describe hybrid Azure Arc/on-prem plus public cloud—while conference mood improved versus prior post-acquisition angst despite smaller attendance.

talks.title: VMware Explore: Broadcom CPO Answers Private AI Questions
talks.teaser: Presenters detail vulnerability discovery and exploitation in VMware Explore: Broadcom CPO Answers Private AI Questions.
talks.summary:
Overview:
Beth Pariseau from Informa TechTarget interviews Paul Turner, Chief Product Officer for Broadcom's VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) division, at VMware Explore in Las Vegas. Turner outlines Broadcom's strategic vision for "Private AI," detailing how enterprises can operationalize artificial intelligence infrastructure from bare metal up to production models within secure private cloud environments. The conversation addresses enterprise data sovereignty, cost predictability, network micro-segmentation, and the shift toward autonomous agentic workflows.

Key Topics:
- Private AI Cloud architecture: From bare metal infrastructure to deployed AI models
- VMware vDefend security extensions, distributed IDS/IPS, and micro-segmentation
- True Source open-source software vetting and platinum CNCF ecosystem collaboration
- AI "tokenomics", GPU capital efficiency, and transitioning to autonomous agent workflows

Technical Details:
Turner outlines the foundational architecture of the Private AI Cloud, which Broadcom conceptualizes as an enterprise "AI Factory." This full-stack infrastructure enables organizations to provision high-performance GPU compute clusters (partnering closely with Nvidia and AMD hardware) alongside virtualized storage and software-defined networking directly within their private data centers. By retaining model fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and inferencing on-premises, enterprises maintain strict data privacy and regulatory sovereignty over proprietary business data, eliminating the data leakage risks inherent in public multi-tenant hyperscaler AI endpoints.

To secure AI execution environments, Broadcom integrated advanced protections into its VMware vDefend platform. vDefend extends distributed intrusion detection and prevention systems (IDS/IPS) and granular network micro-segmentation directly around AI workload clusters, establishing robust East-West inspection perimeters to intercept lateral movement, prompt injection payloads, and unauthorized access to vector databases. Additionally, Turner highlights the True Source initiative, which provides enterprises with cryptographically verified, vulnerability-scanned builds of popular open-source databases and foundational components. Through platinum sponsorship of the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), Broadcom ensures seamless integration with open-weight models and cloud-native toolchains.

The discussion also explores the operational economics of enterprise AI, termed "tokenomics." Turner explains that recurring public cloud API token fees quickly become unsustainable and unpredictable for high-throughput enterprise applications; running right-sized specialized models on dedicated on-premise GPU clusters allows CIOs to establish predictable capital and operational expenditure models. Looking forward to the VCF 9.0 platform release, Turner details the VMware Tanzu agentic control plane, which transitions administrative workflows from simple conversational chatbots to autonomous agents capable of dynamically orchestrating complex enterprise workflows across manufacturing, healthcare, and IT operations.

Key Takeaways:
Private AI architectures allow enterprises to harvest the benefits of generative AI and agentic automation while maintaining absolute control over sensitive intellectual property and compliance boundaries. Security leaders must wrap AI model runtimes and vector stores in micro-segmented perimeters using distributed IDS/IPS tooling to prevent lateral exploitation. Deploying domain-specific, right-sized models on dedicated private infrastructure provides superior cost predictability compared to the volatile tokenomics of public cloud LLM providers.
